Brompton.hq: Greenford, London, UK (a new Ashford, Kent headquarters has been announced)
Brompton.ownership: Private. A 15% stake was sold in June 2026 (per Wikipedia).
Brompton.positioning: Folding bikes for city commuting, built in London, with a growing electric range.
Brompton.dataNote: Founding year: Wikipedia gives June 1976 for the company; other sources say 1975 (the bike's design). Headcount is a Revelio Labs estimate, not a company figure. P&A count is a proxy: one UK dealer (Condor Cycles) stocks about 345 items in its Brompton components, spares and bags range, including some third-party brands (Brooks, SKS, Lezyne). It is not Brompton's own catalogue size.
Brompton.paCategories: Luggage and bags, lights, saddles, grips and pedals, mudguards, pumps and tools, phone mounts, electric-bike chargers and batteries, spare parts

Tern.ownership: Private; subsidiary of Mobility Holdings Ltd
Tern.positioning: Folding, cargo and electric bikes for everyday urban transport.
Tern.dataNote: Wikipedia says its products are sold in 65 countries. No country list was found, so the map is not filled in. Tern states 10 bike lines (BYB, Verge, Link, Eclipse, Node, Roji, HSD, Quick Haul, NBD, Vektron, Short Haul) sold in 65 countries. No unit figure is published; any volume shown is an estimate.
Tern.paCategories: Accessories and parts, partly under sister brand BioLogic

Dahon.hq: Offices in the US, Europe and China
Dahon.ownership: Founded by Dr David T. Hon, who is still CEO per Wikipedia.
Dahon.positioning: Folding bikes; says it ranked first in folding-bike retail volume in mainland China and globally in 2023 (its own claim, citing a CIC report).
Dahon.dataNote: Dahon's own pages quote different country counts (28+, 40+ and 70+). No country list was found, so the map is not filled in. LOW CONFIDENCE: units is the annual output Dahon claims on its own site (1 million, all bike types, not only folding). It is a capacity-style claim, not audited sales. Dahon also states 300+ models across 15 series (folding, e-bikes, kids, carbon). Guinness recognised 500,000+ folding bikes a year in 2008.
Dahon.paCategories: Components and spare parts (patented parts sold alongside bikes)

Ahooga.positioning: Belgian-designed and built 20-inch folding bike (A-MAX) with a patented hinge-free double-triangle frame, upgradeable to electric (E-MAX).
Ahooga.dataNote: Belgian design and manufacture per BIKE Magazin. No founding year, headcount or country list found.

Gocycle.positioning: Premium folding e-bike with a proprietary front-hub motor, single-sided carbon fork and 10-second fold.
Gocycle.dataNote: Press describes Gocycle as made by Karbon Kinetics. Headquarters, founding year and headcount were not confirmed. Current range: G4, G4i and G4i+ (3 models) per UK retailer and press listings.

Birdy.positioning: Full-suspension folding bike designed by Riese & Müller and built by Pacific Cycles in Taiwan.
Birdy.dataNote: CHECK: Wikipedia says Riese & Müller stopped marketing and selling the Birdy in 2025 to focus on e-bikes. Confirm whether the Birdy is still sold (for example by Pacific Cycles) before treating it as an active competitor.
